reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner product space with its normed additive commutative group structure and a measurable space structure whose sigma-algebra is the Borel sigma-algebra, and let d = dim_R E. For every everywhere differentiable function f : E -> R, every eta, beta, lambda in R with eta > 0, beta >= 0 and lambda >= 0, assume that its gradient is globally beta-Lipschitz. For every h, xp in E and every r in R, if ||h - xp|| <= sqrt(d eta) and 12 beta^2 eta^2 lambda^2 <= 1, define mu on E x E as the product of the pushforward of the centered identity-covariance Gaussian measure on E by z -> h + sqrt(eta) z and the pushforward of that same Gaussian measure by z -> sqrt(eta) z. Put theta = (pi/2) r and define F(x,y) = exp(lambda |< (pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h) - sin(theta)y), grad f(xp) - grad f(h + sin(theta)(x-h) + cos(theta)y) >|), where the inner product is real and all scalar-vector products are scalar multiplication in E. Then f has gradient grad f(x) at every x in E, F is measurable and Bochner integrable with respect to mu, integral F dmu <= 2 exp(10 d eta^2 lambda^2 beta^2), and log(integral F dmu) <= log(2) + 10 d eta^2 lambda^2 beta^2. All integrals, exponentials and logarithms in these conclusions are real-valued; r is unrestricted and no positive-dimension assumption is made.
